blocks.md: This lesson follows **Distributed Trajectory Tracing** in *Operating Agents* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Operating Agents, § Distributed Trajectory Tracing
blocks.md: When a trial of `candidate_v2` on the connection-pool repair fails or stalls, aggregate summary metrics record only the wall-clock total and the final verdict, blending remote inference stalls, blocked test containers, and malformed or truncated tool outputs into one undifferentiated number. A trace separates those possibilities by binding every interaction back to the specific evaluation trial, candidate revision, and runtime operation, replacing disjointed service logs with an end-to-end causal record.

questions.q: The section **Distributed Trajectory Tracing** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: An agent incident is diagnosed by keeping findings separated by boundary and testing each with a controlled intervention on the recorded trajectory, not by naming one culprit.
Sampling may thin diagnostic detail but never the accounting record of admitted trials, verdicts, spend, and drops, and retention is chosen per verdict under storage and privacy budgets.

Spans bind every model call, mediated tool execution, and check to their trial and artifact, but a diagnostic trace may sample or drop and never replaces the durable recovery log or the verdict record.
The longest chain of dependent operations recorded in the trace is measured from span timing, and only work on it can shorten the trajectory.
